Thanks for the call earlier today. Quick recap from our side:

- Main goal: validate Redwood inference for our customer support triage pipeline (intent classification + extractive QA)
- Success criteria (high-level):
  1) 95% intent classification accuracy on our test set
  2) Avg 95th-percentile latency < 200ms for streaming responses under 50 RPS
  3) End-to-end cost <$0.015 per 1k tokens
  4) Support for streaming tokens and tool-calling to our ticketing system

Next steps: please send the integration plan, SDK examples, and a proposed timeline for a 4-week POC. We'll confirm infra and legal with procurement.

 Alex
Senior Engineering Manager
Acme Corp

Hi Alex - thanks for the clear recap. We're aligned on the goals. Doc and attachments attached (evaluation matrix + checklist). High level POC plan below and timeline:

POC scope (4 weeks):
- Week 0: Kickoff + environment access (API keys, VPC peering as needed)
- Week 1: SDK integration + sample routes (streaming + sync) - Redwood to provide code snippets and a small sample app
- Week 2: Load/run initial 10k tokens/day, measure latency; implement KV/prefix caching for hot flows
- Week 3: Tool-calling integration to ticketing system (webhook or function call shim) + quality tuning
- Week 4: Final evaluation, cost analysis, handoff

Ownership:
- Redwood: Marissa (POC lead), Connor (integration/SE), Rishi (pricing/ops)
- Acme: Alex (eng lead), Priya (security), Samir (SRE)

Immediate asks for kickoff:
1) API access (we'll issue a short-lived token scoped to the POC)
2) Sample dataset (anonymized) and traffic shape (RPS, token lengths)
3) Confirm whether streaming or blocking first (we recommend streaming for this workflow)

I'll schedule a 30-minute kickoff for Monday morning PST unless you prefer another time.

Regards,

Hi all - following up with technical integration notes and SDK snippets.

1) SDK & routes
- SDKs: python (pip install redwood-sdk), node (npm i @redwood/inference)
- Example route (streaming):
  POST /v1/generate/stream
  Headers: Authorization: Bearer <POC_TOKEN>
  Body: {"model":"redwood-1-stream","input":"<text>","stream":true}

2) Tool calling
- We support a lightweight tool-calling protocol. Example payload for ticket creation:
  {"tool_name":"create_ticket","args":{"subject":"...","body":"...","priority":"P2"}}
- Tool calls can be routed to either a webhook endpoint or executed via the SDK's function registration. We'll provide a sample webhook shim that posts to your ticketing API.

3) Performance & batching
- For low-latency streaming, set batch_size=1 and enable prefix caching for repeated contexts. We'll preconfigure quantized model variant for latency-sensitive flows.

4) Attachments & artifacts
- See attached acme-integration-checklist.pdf and acme-poc-eval-matrix.xlsx. The checklist has step-by-step runbook for peering, token issuance, and test harness.

Next actions:
- Marissa to send kickoff calendar invite for Monday 10am PST
- Acme to share anonymized dataset and RPS profile
- Connor to open a shared Slack channel for real-time debugging

Cheers,
Connor O'Brien
